subject: Post-call: retention & backup SLAs, SOC 2 & vendor Q follow-up
messages:
From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.com>
To: Elena Ruiz <elena.ruiz@summithealthtech.com>, Kyle Barton <kbarton@summithealthtech.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.com>

Subject: Post-call recap: retention windows, backups & next steps

Hi Elena / Kyle —

Thanks for taking the time earlier. Quick recap and concrete next steps so we can keep momentum with procurement/security: 

Summary of what we covered: 
- SOC 2: Redwood is SOC 2 Type II in scope for our hosted API. We maintain the SOC 2 report and can provide an executed NDA copy review process for the report delivery.
- Data residency & GDPR/HIPAA: Hosted deployments support region pinning (US/EU). For HIPAA, we offer BAAs and can deploy to our Private (VPC) option if you require customer-managed networking.
- Retention & deletion policy: Default logs and request artifacts retention is 30 days for standard hosted customers; we can extend retention up to 365 days on Dedicated/Private plans with contractual SLAs. Backups snapshot retention is configurable — typical config options: 30/90/365 days.
- Backups & restores: Backups are incremental snapshots stored encrypted at rest; RTO varies by retention tier (we typically target 4–24 hours for snapshot restores depending on size/region).

Outstanding items / action owners: 
1) Elena/Kyle: send the vendor security questionnaire you mentioned (you said you would share the spreadsheet) — you can drop it here or to security@redwood.com.
2) Redwood (Ben & team): provide a short PDF that summarizes retention windows, backup snapshot lifecycle, and typical RTO/RPO by tier. Also highlight where backups are stored (cloud region) and copy of our deletion flow for customer data.
3) Hannah: schedule a 30-min follow-up next week to walk through the questionnaire and align on SLA language.

Attachments I will circulate from our side in the reply: sample retention policy summary + an example S3 manifest for backups.

Proposed times for a follow-up: Tue 2026-11-24 10:00–11:00 PT or Wed 2026-11-25 09:00–10:00 PT. Let me know what works.

Best,
Hannah Schmitt
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
hannah.schmitt@redwood.com | (415) 555-0193

Subject: Re: Post-call recap: retention windows, backups & next steps

Elena —

Thanks for sending the questionnaire. I (Ben, Security Solutions) will take primary ownership of the VSA. Target: initial pass with answers + supporting artifacts by Thu 2026-11-26 EOD. If you need any items sooner, flag them and we'll prioritize.

Quick clarifications based on your asks: 
- SOC 2: we'll provide the SOC 2 Type II report under NDA. Please confirm the email to send the NDA to and we'll route the report.
- Deletion flow: customer deletion triggers both logical record deletion and a background scrub that removes cached prefixes and KV entries within 24–72 hours; final physical snapshot removal follows the backup retention policy (snapshots older than retention threshold are expired/deleted per lifecycle). We will document the lifecycle steps in the attached PDF.
- Encryption: TLS 1.2+ in transit; AES-256 at rest for snapshots and logs. KMS-managed keys for Private deployments (customer-controlled optional).
- Snapshot restores & index rebuilds: restore includes data/materializing the snapshot; application-level index rebuilds depend on the engine. For typical LLM KV caches + index metadata we budget an additional 1–3 hours for index warm-up for medium-sized data sets (10s GB). We'll include faster warm caches options for Dedicated customers (warm replicas).

I've attached a short retention & snapshot policy summary and an example backup manifest. These are redacted examples; we will provide expanded language for contract attachments if we move to Dedicated/Private.

Attachments: redwood_retention_snapshot_policy.pdf, s3_backup_manifest_example.txt

Best,
Ben Carter
Security Solutions | Redwood Inference

From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>

Looping in a quick ops note from the infra side: 
- RPO: for our standard hosted tier we typically guarantee a 24-hour RPO (point-in-time snapshot frequency depending on workload); for Dedicated we can contract down to 1–4 hour RPOs with more frequent incremental snapshots.
- RTO note: as Ben mentioned, the restore process plus index warm-up is the main driver. For a medium dataset (~50 GB of model KV/cache + logs), expect 3–6 hours from snapshot restore kickoff to an operational-ready state without warm replicas; with warm replica options we can be sub-90 minutes.
- Backup locations: snapshots are stored in the customer region (AWS us-west-2 or us-east-1 for Summit by default) unless the Private deployment requires a specific VPC/on-prem target.

I'll be available on the follow-up call to walk through RTO/RPO numbers in more detail.

-Marcus
